question.text: A public company has conducted its AGM through Video Conferencing. What must the company do with the recorded transcript of the proceedings?

answer.text: File it with SEBI within 30 days of the AGM
Send it to all shareholders by registered post within 15 days
Retain it internally for 8 years without public disclosure
Place it on the company's website (if any) as soon as possible after the AGM

explanation.text: The Logic: For a public company, the workbook states that the recorded transcript of the AGM proceedings shall, as soon as possible, be made available on the company's website, if any. The Trap: Filing with SEBI within 30 days, sending by registered post within 15 days, or retaining only internally for 8 years are not the workbook's stated requirements. The qualifier "if any" on the website is part of the source wording and should not be omitted. Note: The requirement to make the transcript available on the company website (if any) as soon as possible after a public-company AGM is set out on page 160 of the NISM-Series-II-A Registrars and Transfer Agents (Corporate) Certification Examination workbook (October 2025).
